video.title: Build Your Next Business With This Viral AI Tool

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Max Brodeur, co-founder of Y Combinator-backed Gumloop, a drag-and-drop AI workflow automation platform described as an AI-first Zapier. Max demos internal workflows (lead enrichment on signup, support-chat digest, pre-meeting research, SEO keyword filtering, YouTube-to-blog, Meta ads competitor analysis). Chris pitches businesses built on top: Gumloop expert/freelance builder, Facebook ads reverse-engineering as a service, programmatic SEO as a service, white-labelled flows. The key takeaway is that niche workflow knowledge encoded into AI workflows can be sold as a service, but the video is partly promotional (affiliate link) and numbers are sparse.

tactics.name: Automate any task you can write as a list of steps
steps: Pick a task you could hand to an intern as a point-form list
Avoid tasks with many conditionals and edge cases
Encode your expertise and context into the workflow
Keep a human in the loop for high-nuance outputs

quote.text: if you can define something as a list of steps, it's kind of ripe for automation
quote.speaker: Max Brodeur

tactics.name: Use categorisation buckets instead of numeric scoring
steps: Use discrete buckets such as extremely high value, high value, normal, low value
Avoid 0-100 scores because models give mediocre scores when uncertain

quote.text: I tend to do categorization instead of scoring
quote.speaker: Max Brodeur

tactics.name: Match model to task
steps: Use a cheaper fast model for simple high-volume labelling
Use a stronger reasoning model for synthesis over many items
Do not economise on models for high-importance workflows

quote.text: use like a a cheaper model that is faster because sometimes the task is so easy
quote.speaker: Max Brodeur

tactics.name: Find automation opportunities from repetitive Ctrl+F or copy-paste work
steps: Notice repetitive search or copy-paste tasks
Ask whether an LLM could do the reasoning
Build a wrapper or workflow for it

tactics.name: Review drafts before sending; auto-send only templated emails
steps: Save researched, personalised emails as drafts and review
Auto-send only simple templated emails with a calendar link

quote.text: I always save emails as drafts and then I'm the one sending it off.
quote.speaker: Max Brodeur

warnings.warning: Fully autonomous agents have been unreliable and expensive; asking an AI to write a sales email without context yields slop.

quote.text: If you just ask an agent to go write a sales email, it's going to write some slop
quote.speaker: Max Brodeur

warnings.warning: Don't spam people with AI-generated outreach; keep a human in the loop for personalised emails.

quote.text: you never want to be someone spamming or like flooding someone's inbox with more spam
quote.speaker: Max Brodeur

warnings.warning: Templates are a band-aid; screen-recording-based automation discovery may underdeliver and burn user trust.

lessons.lesson: Treat AI like a new employee: give it context, branding and examples, and encode your deep process knowledge into the workflow.

quote.text: I think you need to treat AI like an employee.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Workflows with defined steps beat open-ended agents for near-term reliable business value.
Niche domain knowledge plus tooling is the moat; the value is knowing what to automate, not engineering.

quote.text: It's just a matter of like applying niche knowledge to tooling.
quote.speaker: Max Brodeur

lessons.lesson: Getting in early on a platform ecosystem (as an expert or agency) can be a way to get ahead, but it carries platform risk.
Each automation can be a productised service: look at any internal workflow and ask if it can be sold as a subscription report.

quote.text: every single one of these flows is a business
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Show the customer the outcome, not the tooling: white-label workflows behind a simple form.
Use cheap models for high-volume simple tasks and keep spend on reasoning for high-value steps.
Small teams of exceptional people with AI can move like large companies.

quote.text: one engineer with AI can have can do the the work of 20
quote.speaker: Max Brodeur

evidence_quality.rationale: Product-founder interview with demos; business ideas are mostly the host's hypotheticals with few verified numbers. Gumloop's own growth and usage claims are first-hand but unverified.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host uses a Gumloop affiliate link (says not sponsored); guest is founder of the platform being promoted.
